recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. If future work wants worked examples for canonical targets in cross-version packages, handle that in the extension-pack or xver IG source rather than by adding redundant core versions-page prose.
issue_request: FHIR-44664 was an Applied/Persuasive FHIR-I R6 clarification asking that Basic and cross-version guidance explain that, when cross-version extensions backport newer canonical resources into older FHIR versions, Basic can be treated as the canonical-resource representation and referenced from those extensions.
initial_application: Upstream commit a791ea16e694364b097e029ed44114f67a717832, included in merged PR HL7/fhir#3967, added the active Basic page section 'Basic as a Canonical Resource Wrapper' to source/basic/basic-notes.xml. The section states that Basic can wrap canonical resources absent from the FHIR version being used, can be treated as a canonical resource for referencing, and can be referenced using canonical reference patterns from cross-version extensions.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Basic as an active resource. source/versions.html contains the active cross-version extension package guidance that the Basic note links to. FHIR-I WGM minutes from 2024-02-02 record the canonical/Basic discussion and 20-0-0 vote for FHIR-44664. Related alternate-canonical mechanics are maintained in the FHIR Extension Pack, where FHIR-44663 corrected that extension's value type to url.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current built Basic source conveys the requested rule, and adding another Basic-specific paragraph to the core versions page would duplicate rather than correct implementer guidance.

related_jiras.note: Related WGM discussion and extension-pack history corrected alternate-canonical to use url rather than canonical; it supports the external cross-version mechanism but is not the seed issue.
WGM minutes identify a broader implicit canonical behavior documentation topic, but it is separate from the Basic canonical wrapper clarification.
WGM minutes describe ActorDefinition-in-Basic as a motivating use case; the ticket was not independently reconciled here.
